purpose: Guide a focused feature or experiment specification with testable requirements, controlled exposure, reliable telemetry, decision gates, and safe rollout behavior.

ordered_sections.title: Document control and status
ordered_sections.purpose: Identify ownership, version, lifecycle state, and approval status.

ordered_sections.title: Stakeholder and business source requirements
ordered_sections.purpose: Record the authoritative needs from which use cases and requirements are derived.

ordered_sections.title: Terminology
ordered_sections.purpose: Define stable terms, actors, states, events, and measures.

ordered_sections.title: Problem, value, and evidence
ordered_sections.purpose: Explain the observed problem, affected outcomes, and decision relevance.

ordered_sections.title: Objectives, hypothesis, decision, and non-goals
ordered_sections.purpose: State what the experiment tests, which decision it informs, and what is out of scope.

ordered_sections.title: Scope, personas, eligibility, exclusions, segmentation, and assignment
ordered_sections.purpose: Define who can enter the experiment and how assignment remains interpretable.

ordered_sections.title: Use cases and current, proposed, and treatment flows
ordered_sections.purpose: Describe numbered use cases and observable end-to-end behavior.

ordered_sections.title: Control, treatment, exposure, and contamination controls
ordered_sections.purpose: Define variants, exposure semantics, and protections against cross-variant contamination.

ordered_sections.title: Functional and non-functional requirements
ordered_sections.purpose: Specify atomic, necessary, traceable, prioritized, and verifiable behavior.

ordered_sections.title: Event and property dictionary
ordered_sections.purpose: Define telemetry events, properties, producers, consumers, and expected states.

ordered_sections.title: Funnel and metric definitions
ordered_sections.purpose: Define populations, windows, grains, dimensions, comparators, and calculation rules.

ordered_sections.title: Data-quality and reconciliation checks
ordered_sections.purpose: Specify behavior for missing, duplicate, delayed, inconsistent, and unreconciled telemetry.

ordered_sections.title: Primary, secondary, guardrail metrics, and decision gates
ordered_sections.purpose: Connect measures and quality thresholds to ramp, stop, and final decision rules.

ordered_sections.title: Acceptance, test matrix, and traceability
ordered_sections.purpose: Link source needs, use cases, requirements, scenarios, telemetry, and verification.

ordered_sections.title: Edge, error, accessibility, and failure behavior
ordered_sections.purpose: Define observable behavior outside the primary success path.

ordered_sections.title: Dependencies, risks, assumptions, and tenets
ordered_sections.purpose: Expose conditions and principles that can change delivery or interpretation.

ordered_sections.title: Verification and stakeholder sign-off
ordered_sections.purpose: Assign verification methods, reviewers, and approval state.

ordered_sections.title: Ramp, stop, rollback, analysis, and operational ownership
ordered_sections.purpose: Define safe release controls, analysis timing, recovery, and accountable operators.

narrative_rules: Derive each requirement from an authoritative need and a numbered use case.
Add a requirement only when existing requirements do not cover a valid use case.
Keep each requirement singular, observable, necessary or explicitly optional, prioritized, and verifiable.
Separate stakeholder-driven requirements from system-design requirements.
State the hypothesis, decision, control, treatment, and exposure semantics before interpreting experiment measures.
Describe conditions before required behavior when a condition applies.
Keep objective, mechanism, requirement, acceptance result, telemetry, and decision rule distinct.
Include negative, boundary, accessibility, error, and recovery behavior where applicable.
evidence_rules: Trace every measure to its definition, population, window, grain, dimensions, comparator, source, freshness, and caveat.
Keep actual observations, forecasts, assumptions, targets, and commitments in separate evidence states.
Define treatment exposure independently from downstream outcomes.
Specify detection and handling for missing, duplicate, delayed, or inconsistent telemetry.
Do not permit an experiment decision when required data-quality gates fail.
Link every material claim and decision gate to the claim registry.
terminology_rules: Use stable identifiers for source needs, use cases, requirements, acceptance criteria, tests, events, metrics, dependencies, and variants.
Use one defined term for each actor, eligibility state, exposure, outcome, and guardrail.
Distinguish control, treatment, assignment, eligibility, exposure, conversion, and analysis population.
Expand acronyms at first use unless an approved glossary marks them as established.
formatting_rules: Number use cases, requirements, acceptance criteria, test scenarios, events, metrics, and dependencies for traceability.
Use tables for dictionaries, traceability, test matrices, and aligned variant comparisons.
Keep causal rationale in prose rather than relying on tables alone.
Show lifecycle and approval state for requirements and decisions.
Apply the current organization template before default product-document formatting.
hard_fail_rules: Block publication when exposure is undefined or contamination controls are missing where needed.
Block publication when missing, duplicate, delayed, or inconsistent telemetry has no defined behavior.
Block publication when a requirement is compound, ambiguous, unobservable, unnecessary, or unverifiable.
Block publication when traceability from source need through verification is missing.
Block publication when rollout lacks stop or rollback behavior.
Block publication when evidence is fabricated, untraceable, mislabeled, or missing critical context.
Block publication when body text and tables conflict or a material contradiction remains unresolved.
Block publication when a date, owner, target, fact, or commitment is silently introduced.
Block publication when required overview context is absent without an approved exception.
Block publication when source-specific sample facts appear in a new artifact.
Block publication when language repair changes a requirement, decision, or protected fact.
Block any full-language-conformance status unless the configured bundle, checks, exceptions, and human review are approved.

source_manifest.reference: Supplied focused feature and experiment reference
